result.summary: The image depicts an urban intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure, including continuous sidewalks and a marked zebra crosswalk. However, the environment lacks traffic calming measures and features significant blank building frontage on one corner, which can reduce the sense of security and street activity.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The building on the left corner has a long, windowless wall at street level, reducing natural surveillance and pedestrian interest.

hazards.name: Wide Intersection Radius
hazards.description: The lack of curb extensions results in a wider turning radius for vehicles and a longer exposure time for pedestrians in the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection corners to shorten the crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Add street trees along the sidewalk to provide shade, improve the aesthetic environment, and psychologically narrow the roadway to slow traffic.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: This is a narrow residential street lined with row houses and parallel parked vehicles. The pedestrian environment consists of a narrow sidewalk directly adjacent to the curb with no buffer from the roadway, and visibility is significantly limited by the presence of large parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles, particularly the large SUV, block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground

hazards.name: Narrow Walkway
hazards.description: The sidewalk appears to be less than 4 feet wide, which may restrict mobility for users with assistive devices or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: The paved area between the house steps and the curb

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Removing parking spaces near intersections or mid-block access points to improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Adding street trees would provide a vertical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway while also helping to naturally slow traffic speeds.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Installing street lights would improve safety and security for pedestrians during nighttime hours.

result.summary: This is a narrow residential street with continuous sidewalks and row housing. While the narrow roadway naturally limits vehicle speeds, the high density of parked cars creates visual obstructions and there is no physical buffer between the walkway and the travel lane.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Large parked SUVs and trucks block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the travel lane, increasing risk during mid-block crossings.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The narrow sidewalk is immediately adjacent to parked cars and the travel lane with no planting strip or physical barrier to protect pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Visible on both sides of the street.

interventions.title: Daylighting at Intersections
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near the ends of the block to improve visibility for pedestrians and drivers at crossing points.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install vertical speed control measures to ensure low vehicle speeds on this narrow residential street.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Add more street trees or planters where space allows to create a vertical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide but poorly defined paved area that lacks a protective curb or buffer from the roadway. A prominent utility pole sits in the middle of the walking path, creating a significant physical obstruction, while blank walls and fences limit passive surveillance.

hazards.name: Utility pole obstruction
hazards.description: A large wooden utility pole is positioned directly in the center of the paved pedestrian area, forcing people to walk around it.

hazards.name: Lack of vertical separation
hazards.description: There is no raised curb or physical barrier between the roadway and the pedestrian walkway, increasing the risk of vehicle encroachment.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground at the edge of the asphalt

interventions.title: Curb and Gutter Installation
interventions.description: Installing a raised curb would clearly define the edge of the roadway and provide a physical barrier for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Moving the utility pole to the edge of the right-of-way or undergrounding utilities would clear the walking path of obstructions.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Adding a planting strip with trees would provide a buffer from traffic and improve the aesthetic and environmental quality of the walk.
